answer: The kidneys maintain blood pH at ~7.4 by tubular secretion of $\text{H}^+$ ions into the filtrate and reabsorption of $\text{HCO}_3^-$ (bicarbonate) back into the blood. answer:
The kidneys regulate blood water and salt content by adjusting urine concentration:
• When water is in excess → low ADH → less water reabsorbed → **hypotonic** (dilute) urine.
• When water is scarce → high ADH → more water reabsorbed → **hypertonic** (concentrated) urine.
Aldosterone promotes $\text{Na}^+$ reabsorption in the DCT, further controlling osmotic balance.
